en.headline: DH and police arrest two after seizing unregistered injections
en.dek: Health officials said more than 50 suspected unregistered injections were taken from over 13 premises in a joint operation tied to advertised multi-cancer WT1 shots.
body: The Department of Health and the police have arrested two people and seized more than 50 suspected unregistered injections from over 13 premises, the department said on Wednesday, as officers continued an investigation into shots marketed as a Wilms tumour 1, or WT1, vaccine claimed to prevent multiple cancers.

Assistant Director of Health Frank Chan said the injections recovered so far were mostly healthcare products such as vitamins and were classified as Part 1 poisons. Authorities had not found the WT1 product in the raids, he said, and there had been no reports of adverse reactions. The operation remained under way and further arrests were possible.

Local reports said the searches, carried out over several days with police, included a medical centre in Lippo Sun Plaza on Canton Road in Tsim Sha Tsui. A 28-year-old clinic supervisor and a woman were arrested on suspicion of illegally selling or possessing unregistered pharmaceutical products and Part 1 poisons. The department has said WT1 is not a registered pharmaceutical product in Hong Kong and that it has found no matching registration with mainland or overseas regulators.

Under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance, illegally selling or possessing an unregistered pharmaceutical product or a Part 1 poison is punishable by a maximum fine of HK$100,000 and two years imprisonment per offence. The department has previously referred the advertising of the shots to the Medical Council and notified Customs over possible illegal importation. It has urged the public not to use unregistered products.

zh.headline: 衞生署聯同警方拘兩人 檢逾50支未註冊針劑
zh.dek: 衞生署表示，就有醫療中心宣傳可預防多種癌症的WT1針劑，聯同警方搜查逾13個處所，檢獲50多支懸疑未經註冊注射劑，兩人被捕。
body: 衞生署周三表示，署方聯同警方採取行動，在超過13個處所檢獲50多支懸疑未經註冊注射劑，並拘捕兩人。行動與有醫療中心在網上宣傳可提供聲稱能預防多種癌症的WT1針劑有關，署方正繼續調查。
衞生署助理署長（藥物）陳凌峯表示，目前檢獲的針劑多數屬維他命等保健製品，並屬第1部毒藥。行動中暫未搜獲WT1製品，至今亦未接獲市民接種後出現不良反應的報告。他指調查仍在進行，不排除再有人被捕。
報道指連日搜查包括尖沙嘲廣東道力寶太陽廣場一間醫療中心，被捕者包括一名28歲診所主管及一名女子，涉嫌非法售賣或管有未經註冊藥劑製品及第1部毒藥。衞生署早前強調，WT1並非香港註冊藥劑製品，亦未發現內地或海外藥品監管機構有相關註冊紀錄。
根據《藥劑業及毒藥條例》，非法售賣或管有未經註冊藥劑製品或第1部毒藥，每項罪行最高可處罰款10萬元及監禂兩年。署方較早時已將有關廣告轉介醫務委員會，並通報海關跟進懸疑非法進口，同時呼籲市民切勿使用未經註冊藥劑製品。
